events.comment: Leaf_Ranger_Boss: the Leaf Ranger fight. The scene links Player_Movement and Combat_Shared before this sheet. He keeps his distance and fights with a fixed rotation of attacks per phase (RotP1, RotP2), plus reactions: a stab when the player is close, an escape slide or a leap over when crowded, a dodge roll on every DodgeEvery-th nearby swing, and a thorn wall after WallHits quick hits.
Scene start: set his speed and start his timers. He waits a moment in Intro before fighting.
Leaf Ranger sounds: one helper for every bow and volley sound. USE picks the set: the arrow pack (default) or our synthesized ones.
His state clock: StateT counts the seconds since the current state or step started.

Keep the enemy bars just above his head. His frame is 288x128 with the body in the lower middle, so the bars follow his head, not the frame top. Raised 22 px, about a quarter of his height, so they clear his face.
The player is gone: stand idle.
Final death: play the death animation and leave the body on its last frame. Arrows in flight and thorns are cleared.
Safety net: no lives left, but he is not in his death state, so die now.
Lost a life: leap to the far side of the arena, hold a pose, then start phase 2. He cannot be hit during this.
Player on the left half: land on the right.
Player on the right half: land on the left.

Posture broken: cancel everything and kneel. He can always be hit while kneeling, even if the break came during a thorn wall or another move that made him invulnerable. Combat_Shared runs the stun and the deathblow.
Stun over: get up and carry on. A deathblow that took a life is handled by the lost-life event above.
A lunge landed: flinch, unless he is in the air, stunned, leaping, on or falling from the sniper perch, or dead.
Dodged a swing: roll away from the player.

Dodge decision: every DodgeEvery-th swing near him, while he is standing in Neutral and the dodge is off cooldown, he dodges it. After each dodge DodgeEvery is re-rolled between 2 and 5, so the player can't count it out.
This is the swing he dodges.
Count the player's hits for the thorn wall. Hits more than WallWindow seconds apart start the count over.
Hits too far apart: start the count over.
Remember his HP for the hit count next frame.

Mini-stagger (fragile): MiniHits quick hits within WallWindow make him flinch with the take-hit animation, a free opening for the player. It resets the hit count, and is off cooldown only every StaggerCooldown seconds, so he can't be stun-locked; while it is on cooldown the hits keep counting toward the thorn wall instead. Only from ground states he can be interrupted in.

Thorn wall: after WallHits quick hits, with the wall off cooldown and him on the ground, he cancels what he is doing and grows vines in front of him. It is a trap for button-mashing: hitting the vines snares the player.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Intro: after a moment, start fighting.
Neutral: face the player.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.

The player is rooted after an entangle, a snare, the thorn wall or the Bramble Grasp: punish it, ignoring cooldowns. Close, he slides straight in and stabs. Further than PunishRainRange, he rains arrows on them. Also straight from the window after the wall.
Far away: one arrow rain on the rooted player, even in phase 2. The rotation then skips its next rain, so two rains do not come back to back.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Close: slide in and stab.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
The root ended before he could use it: forget the punish.
Overgrowth, once in phase 2 below OverHP percent HP: he leaps to the edge farther from the player.
Player on the left half: go to the right edge.
Player on the right half: go to the left edge.

Sniper perch: once in phase 2, below PerchHP percent HP, he leaps onto the branch farther from the player. Up there he cannot be hit: he shoots aimed arrows and, after PerchShots of them, a laser angled down at the player. Deflecting the laser is the only way to knock him down. F4 forces the move for testing.
Player on the left half: he takes the right branch.
Player on the right half: he takes the left branch.
Leaping right: face right.
Leaping left: face left.
Sniper perch: debug, F4 sends him up to the perch from Neutral, in either phase. Remove before release.
Sniper perch: the leap, an arc from the ground up to the branch over PerchLeapTime seconds, PerchArc px above the straight line.

parameters: Leaf_Ranger.Variable(GroundCY) + ((Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchFeetY) - 124) - Leaf_Ranger.Variable(GroundCY)) * min(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(StateT) / Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchLeapTime)) - Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchArc) * 4 * min(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(StateT) / Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchLeapTime)) * (1 - min(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(StateT) / Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchLeapTime)))

events.comment: Arrived: stand on the branch and start the perch routine.
Sniper perch: on the branch he always faces the player.
Player to his right: face right.
Player to his left: face left.
Sniper perch: every PerchShotGap seconds, an aimed shot, until PerchShots have gone.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Sniper perch: on frame 8 the arrow leaves the bow, aimed at the player. It is a diagonal arrow, so it can be deflected and grows a thorn bush where it lands.
Sound: the diagonal arrow whistling down from the branch, just after the release.
Sound: the bow's release, from the branch.
Facing right: the right-facing arrow, turned to the aim angle (its art points 45 degrees down).
Facing left: the left-facing arrow, turned to the aim angle (its art points 135 degrees).
Sniper perch: shot finished, back to waiting on the branch.
Sniper perch: after PerchShots arrows, the laser. The crouch and green star are the tell, as on the ground.

Sniper perch: on frame 3 he takes aim at the player's body. The laser will run from his bow through that spot down to the floor, and a shadow grows where it will hit the ground. The aim point is kept at least 40 px below his bow and the landing point near the arena, so a player jumping up to his height cannot send the laser sideways off the screen.

parameters: clamp(Leaf_Ranger.Variable(BeamBX) + (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(TargetX) - Leaf_Ranger.Variable(BeamBX)) * (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(BeamEY) - Leaf_Ranger.Variable(BeamBY)) / max(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(TargetY) - Leaf_Ranger.Variable(BeamBY)), -300, 1580)

events.comment: Sniper perch: on frame 9 the laser fires along the aimed line, one stretched and rotated beam with one rotated hitbox. DeflectBlocked is cleared first, so a deflect of this laser can be told apart. His animation jumps to frame 13: frames 9 to 12 draw the ground laser straight ahead, which would show a second, wrong laser up here.
Sniper perch: the laser was deflected. He is knocked off the branch: he can be hit again, takes PerchPostureDamage posture, and falls toward the middle.
Sniper perch: the laser was not deflected. Back to shooting arrows from the branch.

Sniper perch: the fall, over PerchFallTime seconds. He lands hard, with a screen shake, and drops into the posture-break kneel for PerchStunTime seconds: the punish window. His posture is not actually broken (no deathblow), unless the knockdown filled it, which starts a real break instead.

parameters: (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchFeetY) - 124) + (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(GroundCY) - (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchFeetY) - 124)) * min(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(StateT) / Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchFallTime)) * min(1, Leaf_Ranger.Variable(StateT) / Leaf_Ranger.Variable(PerchFallTime))

events.comment: Landed: back on the ground with physics on, kneeling as if posture-broken, with a screen shake.
Sniper perch: stun over, back to his normal fight.
Neutral, player close: stab when it is off cooldown.
Neutral, player crowding him: escape. Slide away if there is room behind him, otherwise leap over the player.
Room behind him (the slide must end at least WallMargin from the wall): slide away from the player.
Moving right: face right.
Moving left: face left.
Too close to the wall behind him: slide toward the player instead, straight through them to the open side.
Moving right: face right.
Moving left: face left.
Cornered: leap over the player and land LeapLand past them.
Neutral: when the action delay for this phase is over, take the next attack from the rotation.
Phase 1: wait ActionDelayP1, then read the next code from RotP1.
Phase 2: wait ActionDelayP2, then read the next code from RotP2.
He just punished with a rain: skip this R and take the next code straight away.
Any other move clears the skip, so a later R is not lost.
Code S: Shot.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code E: Entangle shot.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code P: Poison shot.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code R: Arrow rain.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code A: Air volley.
Code Q: Air triple poison. He leaps up like the air volley, then fires a fan of three poison arrows at the player.
Code W: Air triple entangle. The same, with three entangle arrows.
Code B: Beam.
Code D: delayed shot. He holds the full draw for ShotHold seconds before letting go.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code X: double shot. Two arrows ShotGap seconds apart, so the second one needs a chained deflect.
Sound: the string being drawn (it ends about when the arrow leaves, 0.56 s in).
Code G: Bramble Grasp. Roots erupt under where the player stood when he raised his bow.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Neutral, player far away: run toward them.
Player to the right.
Player to the left.
Neutral, at a good distance: stand.
Delayed shot: on frame 7, at full draw just before the release rings, hold for Hold seconds.
Delayed shot: the hold is over, so let go.
Shot: on frame 8, with the green release rings the arrow leaves the bow. A delayed shot holds before this (below), and a double shot sends its second arrow ShotGap seconds later.
Double shot: ShotGap seconds after the first arrow, the second one.
Create an arrow at the bow when one is asked for. Its kind sets its damage and colour.
Sound: the bow's release (every ground shot, the second of a double shot too).
Damage by kind: a normal shot.
Damage by kind: entangle, tinted green.
Damage by kind: poison, tinted purple.
Facing right: the right-facing arrow.
Facing left: the left-facing arrow.
Shot finished: back to Neutral, and the action delay starts now.
Stab: frames 5 to 7 thrust the arrow forward. A melee hitbox covers 160 px in front of him for that time, so a deflect costs him posture.
Stab finished: back to Neutral and start the stab cooldown.
Arrow rain: on frame 9 the volley goes up. Mark where the player is now. Phase 2 sends a second rain RainGap seconds later, wherever the player is then. A shadow grows where it will land.
Sound: a quick spread of releases as the volley goes up, and the whoosh of it coming down (it lands about 0.57 s later).
A punish rain falls once, in either phase.
Arrow rain: RainDelay seconds after the volley, the arrows come down at the marked spot. The shadow goes as it lands.
Arrow rain, phase 2: RainGap seconds later, a second rain at the player's new spot. It gets its own shadow.
Sound: the second rain's whoosh as it comes down.
Arrow rain finished: the volley animation is over and every rain has been sent.

Rain: two hits, as the first arrows land (frame 3) and as the last ones do (frame 9), each its own hitbox HitW wide and 200 px high, for RainTickDamage each. Each can be deflected or taken on its own.
Sound: the volley landing, with the first hit (one sound covers both hits).
Rain, second hit.
Rain: remove it when its brambles have faded.
Air volley: rise AirHeight over AirRise seconds.
At the top: shoot.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Air volley: on frame 6, three diagonal arrows at different speeds, so they land in a spread toward the player.
Sound: the three arrows whistling down.
Sound: three releases, one per arrow.
Create the three arrows at the bow.
Give each its speed and direction.
Right-facing arrow.
Left-facing arrow.
Air combo (AirKind poison or entangle): on frame 6, a fan of three aimed arrows.
Sound: the three arrows whistling down.
Sound: three releases, one per arrow.
Create the three arrows at the bow.
Create the three arrows at the bow.

Aim each new arrow at the ground around the player: the three land AirSpread apart (X --- X --- X, left of them, at them, right of them), at 75% of the ground shot speed. They tilt along their flight. Kind is the air combo's kind (poison or entangle), which sets the damage, tint and the effect on a hit, exactly as for ground shots; where they land, poison leaves a cloud and entangle a vine.

Leaf_Ranger.Variable(ShotSpeed) * 0.75 * sin(atan2(Leaf_Ranger.Variable(GroundCY) + 124 - Ranger_Arrow.Y(), Player.CenterX() + (Leaf_Ranger.Variable(DiagSlot) - 1) * Leaf_Ranger.Variable(AirSpread) - Ranger_Arrow.X()))

events.comment: Poison: its damage, tinted purple.
Entangle: its damage, tinted green.
Right-facing arrow.
Left-facing arrow.
Air volley: shot done, fall back down.
Air volley: falling, over AirFall seconds.
Landed: back on the ground and back to Neutral.

Beam: the crouch and the growing green star on frames 3 to 9 are the tell. On frame 9 the beam fires across the whole arena at chest height: three beam segments and one hitbox to the wall. Roll through it or deflect it.
Create three segments from the edge of his frame.
Line them up end to end.
Beam to the right.
Beam to the left.
Bramble Grasp tell: the red warning kanji, as on the Samurai's grab, sits centred above his bars while the tell lasts. It means: no deflect, get out of the way.
The warning goes if the grasp is interrupted.
Bramble Grasp: GraspDelay seconds after the bow goes up, roots erupt under the marked spot and the warning goes.
Bramble Grasp finished: back to Neutral.

Bramble: while the roots rise (frames 3 to 7 of the grow) they catch a player standing in them. This is a grab: it cannot be deflected, only stepped or rolled out of. Caught means rooted for GraspRootTime, GraspDamage HP, and the punish.

Bramble Grasp roots that caught the player: grow again from the other side, like a second lash. It is the same hit, so no extra damage or root time. They stay on its last frame while the player struggles.
Bramble Grasp roots that missed: fade straight away.
Bramble Grasp roots: the player broke free, so the second lash fades.
Bramble Grasp roots: remove them once faded.
Overgrowth vines: remove them when their animation ends.
Beam: remove the segments when they fade.
Beam finished: back to Neutral.
Thorn wall: from frame 6 the vines are up. Standing near them is safe.
Thorn wall trap: an attack or lunge that hits the vines snares the player in roots for RootTime seconds and costs WallDamage HP. When the vines drop, he slides in for the punish stab.
Thorn wall: the vines pull back on frame 15, so he can be hit again.

Thorn wall finished: he stays open for WallOpenTime seconds in his idle stance. This is the punish window. (The pack's defend_pose frame has the vines up, so it made the wall look like it went back up.)
Punish window over: back to Neutral.
Slide: move away at SlideSpeed until SlideDist is covered or the arena edge is reached, then slow down.

parameters: clamp(Leaf_Ranger.X() + Leaf_Ranger.Variable(MoveDir) * Leaf_Ranger.Variable(SlideSpeed) * TimeDelta(), Leaf_Ranger.Variable(ArenaMinX), Leaf_Ranger.Variable(ArenaMaxX))

events.comment: Entry done: keep sliding in the loop.
Far enough, or at the edge: come out of the slide.
Punish slide: slide toward the player at SlideSpeed.

parameters: clamp(Leaf_Ranger.X() + Leaf_Ranger.Variable(Facing) * Leaf_Ranger.Variable(SlideSpeed) * TimeDelta(), Leaf_Ranger.Variable(ArenaMinX), Leaf_Ranger.Variable(ArenaMaxX))

events.comment: Entry done: keep sliding in the loop.
In range: stab.
The player broke free first: stop and go back to Neutral.
Snare trail: every TrapGap px of an escape slide, up to TrapCount times, he leaves a root trap behind him.
Sliding right: trap facing right.
Sliding left: trap facing left.
Slide finished: face the player again.
Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Dodge roll: move away at RollSpeed for the length of the roll.

Player on his right: face right.
Player on his left: face left.
Flinch over: back to Neutral.
Leap: an arc from FromX to ToX over LeapTime seconds, LeapHeight high, facing the way he jumps.

On the left edge: column 0.

Overgrowth wave: every WaveGap seconds he spins and sends a volley up. The gap starts at the far wall and moves one column toward him each wave, so the player has to follow it, or roll through a rain.

Overgrowth wave: on frame 9 the volley goes up, and dark arrow shadows grow on the ground under every column that is about to be hit, leaving the gap clear. Wait OverRainDelay seconds before the rain comes down.
Sound: the releases as the wave's volley goes up, and its whoosh timed to end as it lands (OverRainDelay later, plus two rain frames).

events.comment: Overgrowth wave: the rain falls on every column but the gap, each rain squeezed to its column and hitting the whole of it, so only the gap is safe. The ground marks are removed as it lands. WaveGap counts from here. Each rain's hitbox stops OverHitMargin px short of its column edges, so a swing from inside the gap, which pushes the player's own hitbox forward, does not reach the rain next to it.
Create one rain per column.
Put each new rain on its column.
Grow vines with this column's rain, squeezed to the column like the rain. They cannot catch anyone.
